title: Retopology (ver 5.1.0)
content: ### ### ### ### ### Objective Draw topology lines on a pattern and create a new mesh. ### **Create** ### Location 3D/2D Window Tool Bar▶ Topology tool ### Operation 1. Follow the path indicated in Location above. 2. With Topology tool selected, patterns will be displayed transparent. \- When you place the mouse cursor over a pattern, the pattern is highlighted in its original color. \- A topology can only be created in one pattern at a time. 3. Click on the highlighted pattern to add a topology point. \- Topology can be created in both 2D and 3D windows. ** Creating Face** \- When creating Topology lines, the Topology face is created if it is a closed shape. \- Topology faces are created only on shapes with 3 or 4 points. \- To create an open shape, double click to finish creating. **Cancel point creation** \- Cancel one by one: Press Delete, Backspace Key on the keyboard. \- Cancel all points: Press ESC, Ctl + Z Key on the keyboard. **Loop Face Division** \- While selecting Topology tool, press Shift + Ctrl and mouse over to add Loop Face Division along the closest topology line. ### Editing ### Location 3D/2D Windows Tool Bar ▶ Edit topology tool ### Operation 1. Follow the path indicated in the Location above. 2. A pattern is highlighted in sky blue after selecting edit topology tool and place the mouse cursor over a pattern. 3. Select Topology point, line, face, and edit. ** Point/ Line multi-selection ** \- While pressing Shift Key on the keyboard and click to select multiple topology points/ lines. **2D point drag selection ** \- While pressing Ctrl key on the keyboard and drag to select multiple topology points. **Line loop selection ** \- Double click a topology line to loop select.** Delete Point/ Line/ Face** \- Press Delete key on the keyboard or right-click and select the delete menu to delete Point/ Line/ Face. **Extrude ** \- Select lines, press Shift + Ctrl and drag to Extrude. **Right-click popup menu ** \- Right-click on a point, line, face, pattern or background to access the popup menus. \- The menu that appears may vary depending on what is applied. **Delete** | Delete selected object. ---|--- **Merge** | Merge two or more points. **Merge All** | Merge all topology points by distance. Set the distance between topology points and click the apply button to merge. Click the close button to close the dialog. **Add Division (Current Pattern)** | Add division on a selected pattern. Adds one division level at a time. **Add All Division ** | Add division to entire Topology face. (right-click on the background to pop-up this menu) **Remesh (duplicate)** | Duplicate a new mesh based on created topology face. (Applied per pattern) **Remesh All (duplicate) ** | Duplicate a new mesh based on created topology face of the entire pattern. **Remesh (replace) ** | Delete an existing pattern and create a new mesh based on created topology face. (Applied per pattern) **Remesh All (replace) ** | Delete the entire pattern and create new mesh based on created topology face. **Show/Hide** Show/Hide created Topology from 3D Main menu ▶ Display ▶3D garment ▶ Show topology. **Topology Ghost Display/Snapping Based on The Sewing Lines (Above Ver.11)** When there are topology points at a pattern edge with a sewing line, you can find the ghosts of those points automatically displayed at the opposite sewing line. These ghost topology points help you snap any new topology you create across sewing relationships to exactly the same place as your existing topology. ### ### Patch Topology (Above Ver.11) ### Location 2D Window Tool Bar ▶ Patch Topology Tool ### Operation 1. Follow the Location above. 2. Select the Edit Patch Topology Tool, and a pop-up box appears, where you can adjust the number of subdivisions. Subdivisions | Adjust the number of subdivisions ---|--- Create | After all of the sections are closed, click the 'Create' button, and the patch lines will turn into topology faces. Clear | Delete all in-progress patch lines. 3. Create patch lines on a 2D pattern. \- Internal topology dash lines will appear divided into the preset number of subdivisions, if a patch section is either triangular or rectangular. \- You can change the number of subdivisions before closing a patch section. \- You can also change the number of subdivisions after closing a patch section by selecting the completed patch line.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for using the Topology tool to draw topology lines, create meshes, and edit topology points and faces within 2D and 3D design environments.

title: Retopology (ver. 12 & Above)
content: ### Objective Allow the user to draw topology lines onto existing patterns creating a new mesh with a lower polygon count and edge-loops optimized for animation. **Create Topology** **Location** 3D/2D Window Tool Bart ▶ Topology Tools **** **Operation** 1. Follow the path indicated in Location above. 2. When a Topology tool selected, patterns will be displayed as transparent. **→** When you place the mouse cursor over a pattern, the pattern is highlighted in its original color. **→** New topology can only be created on one pattern at a time. 3. Click on the highlighted pattern to add a topology point. **→** Topology can be created in both the 2D and 3D Windows, though we recommend using the 2D Window primarily. ** Creating Face** **→** When creating Topology lines, a Topology face is created if a closed shape is drawn. **→** Topology faces are created only on shapes with 3 or 4 points/sides. **→** To stop drawing Topology before closing a shape (leaving an open shape), double-click to finish. **Cancel point creation** **→** Cancel points one-by-one by pressing Delete/Backspace Key on the keyboard. **→** Cancel all points: Press ESC, Ctl + Z Key on the keyboard. **Add Division Loop** **→** While hovering over an edge with the Create Topology Tool, press Shift + Ctrl and click to add an edge loop across continuous faces. **Additional Operation (Above Ver.12)** **Cut Topology Faces →** Existing blue topology faces can be split by drawing new Topology Points/Edges across them.** →** If cut faces result in Ngons, any blue topology faces with more than 4 sides will be highlighted in orange. **Edit Topology** **Location** 3D/2D Windows Tool Bar▶ Edit Topology Tool **Operation** 1. Follow the path indicated in the Location above. 2. Existing topology is highlighted in sky blue after selecting the Edit Topology Tool and 3. Place the mouse cursor over a pattern with existing topology. 4. Select a Topology point, line, or face, and edit it by holding and moving it, or deleting it with the Delete Key. ** Point/ Line** **/ Face ****multi-selection ****→** While holding the Shift or the Ctrl Key, click on multiple topology points/lines one at a time to add them to a selection. **2D point drag selection ****→** While pressing Ctrl key on the keyboard and drag to select multiple topology points. **Line loop selection ****→** Double click a topology line to loop select.** Delete Point/ Line/ Face** **→** Press Delete key on the keyboard or right-click and select the delete menu to delete Point/ Line/ Face.** ** **Extrude ****→** Select lines, press Shift + Ctrl and drag to Extrude. **Right-click popup menu ****→** Right-click on a point, line, face, pattern or background to access the popup menus. **→** The menu that appears may vary depending on what is applied. Delete | Delete selected object. ---|--- Show Topology Only (3D) | Display only the topology, excluding garments or other objects. Show All | Unhide everything in the scene in 3D window. Merge | Merge two or more points. Merge All | Merge all topology points by distance. Set the distance between topology points and click the apply button to merge. Click the close button to close the dialog. Add Division (Current Pattern) | Add division on a selected pattern. Adds one division level at a time. Add All Division | Add division to entire Topology face. (right-click on the background to pop-up this menu) Remesh (duplicate) Convert (Duplicate) (ver. 2024.0) | Duplicate a new mesh based on created topology face. (Applied per pattern) Remesh All (duplicate) Convert All (Duplicate) (ver. 2024.0) | Duplicate a new mesh based on created topology face of the entire pattern. Remesh (replace) Convert (Replace) (ver. 2024.0) | Delete an existing pattern and create a new mesh based on created topology face. (Applied per pattern) Remesh All (replace) Convert All (Replace) (ver. 2024.0) | Delete the entire pattern and create new mesh based on created topology face. ** Show/ Hide** **→** Show/ Hide created Topology from 3D Main menu ▶ Display ▶3D garment ▶ Show topology. **Topology Ghost Display/Snapping Based on The Sewing Lines (Above Ver.11) ****→** When Topology Points meet pattern edges with a sewing line, you can find the ghosts of those points automatically displayed at the opposite sewing relationship.** ****→** These ghost Topology Points help you snap any new topology you create across sewing relationships to exactly the same place as the existing topology on patterns across the seam. **Additional Operation (Above Ver.12)** **Topology Ghost Display/Snapping across Sewing Relationships for Internal Lines ****→** When Topology Points meet Internal Lines with a sewing line, you can find the ghosts of those points automatically displayed at the opposite sewing relationship. **Drag Select Topology Points ** → Click outside of an area of blue topology and drag across it to select multiple Topology Points at once.** **→ Click and hold the 'Shift' Key, then click and drag over an additional area of blue topology to add Topology Points to an existing selection. **Drag Deselect Topology Points ** → Click and hold the 'Control' Key, then click and drag over an existing selection of Topology Points to remove Topology Points from that selection. **Patch Topology** **Location** 2D Window Tool Bar ▶ Patch Topology Tool **Operation(Above Ver.11)** 1. Navigate to the interface/menu Location above. 2. Select the 'Patch Topology' Tool, and a pop-up box will appear where you can adjust the number of subdivisions for an edge. Subdivisions | Adjust the number of edge subdivisions ---|--- Patch Style (ver. 2024.1) | Grid | Grid is the legacy algorithm which obtains more linear results. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438108949529)![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438125656473)![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438080407961) Uniform | A new algorithm which obtains results with more natural flow and smaller size differences. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438080642073)![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438094654617) Create | After the patch shape is closed, click the 'Create' button, and the patch lines will turn into topology faces. Clear | Delete all in-progress patch lines. 3. Create patch lines on a 2D pattern. **→** Internal topology will appear divided into the preset number of subdivisions along edges, if a a closed patch section is either triangular or rectangular. **→** You can change the number of subdivisions for the next edge while a Topology Patch is in progress (before the patch shape is closed). **→** You can also change the number of subdivisions after closing a patch section (but before clicking 'Create') by selecting the completed patch edge and changing the number in the 'Subdivisions' field. **Additional Operation (Above Ver.12)** **Snap Patch Topology to Internal Shapes/Lines** **→** Patch Topology edges will snap to both external and internal pattern lines and curve points. **Snap Patch Topology to Convex Curves** **→** Patch Topology edges will now snap to both concave and convex curves. **→** If the curvature of an edge is too extreme for a patch to be created, add one or several curve points along the curved edge with the 'Add Point/Split Line' tool to divide the curve into sections with less extreme curvature. **Evaluate Patch Validity at Creation** **→** After closing a Topology Patch and clicking 'Create', if the drawn patch would create overlapping geometry, an error window pop-up will be raised - return to the Patch Topology tool and update the patch as necessary to avoid overlapping edges/vertices. **→** If the drawn patch would not result in overlapping geometry, the Topology Patch will be created and displayed in blue. ※ Note: * The algorithm for patch topology has been improved, resulting in a more efficient mesh. (ver. 2024.0) * In the case of a square with the same number of points on each side, the results for both Grid and Uniform patch styles are the same. (ver. 2024.1)
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to create and edit optimized topology lines on existing patterns, enabling the generation of lower polygon count meshes suitable for animation.

title: Apply Fabric
content: ### Objective Apply Fabrics (.zfab) to Patterns. ### Operation #### Apply from Property Editor 1. Click on a Pattern, and choose a Fabric to apply from the Fabric menu in the Property Editor. → The selected Fabric is now being applied to the selected Pattern accordingly. ※ Note: * Only Fabrics in the Fabric tab are being displayed in the corresponding Fabric menu. #### Assign to Selected Pattern 1. Select a Pattern. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Assign to Selected Patterns → The selected Fabric is now being applied to the selected Pattern accordingly. #### Assign to New Fabric 1. Select a Pattern. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric ▶ Assign to New Fabric Right-click Pattern Pop-up Menu ▶ Assign to New Fabric → The new Fabric is now being applied to the selected Pattern and simultaneously added on the Fabric tab. #### Apply from Folder 1. With Window File Search, open a folder where the Fabric files are being stored. 2. Drag and drop a desired Fabric onto a pattern in 2D or 3D window. → The selected Pattern is now being applied to the selected Pattern and simultaneously added on the Fabric tab. 3. Or, drag and drop Fabric files onto Fabric tab of the Object Browser. → In case of drag-and-dropping onto Fabric item, the previous Fabric style gets replaced. → In case of drag-and-dropping onto the empty space, the Fabric gets added in the list. #### Apply from Library Window 1. Open a folder where the Fabric files are being stored from the Library window. 2. Drag and drop a desired Fabric onto a Pattern in 2D or 3D window. → The selected Pattern is now being applied to the selected Pattern and simultaneously added on the Fabric List window. 3. Drag and drop fabric files onto Fabric tab of the Object Browser: → In case of drag-and-dropping onto Fabric item, the previous item gets replaced. → In case of drag-and-dropping onto the empty space, the Fabric gets added in the list. #### Apply from Fabric Tab 1. Drag and drop a desired Fabric onto a Pattern in 2D or 3D window. → The selected Pattern is now being applied to the selected Pattern.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to apply various fabrics to patterns using multiple methods within the software.

title: 3D Garment (*.zpac) Open/Add/Save
content: ### **Objective** Save the 3D Garment and 2D Pattern contents together in a *.zpac file format. Save the Garment to the user’s computer, or open and edit a saved Garment file. ### **Location** #### Open Garment Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open ▶ Garment #### Add Garment Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Add ▶ Garment #### Save Garment Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Save As ▶ Garment #### New Garment (ver. 12.1) Main Menu ▶ File ▶ New Garment (Ctrl+Shift+N) ### **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: 2. Select the desired file and click Open to load it. ※ Note: * Garment files (*.zpac) and Project files (*.zprj) can be opened by double clicking them or dragging and dropping them onto the 3D window. * #### Open Auto Save File If the program is closed abnormally while a Garment is being worked on, a pop-up window saying “Autosave file exists, do you want to recover the autosave file?” appears when the program runs again. Click Yes to load the autosave file or click No to refrain from loading the autosave file. (Project File (*.zprj) is auto saved from ver3.1.0.) ### ### **Open or Add** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open / Add ▶ Garment 2. Select a Garment file and click Open. → The Add Garment window appears (ver2.4.0) 3. Select the appropriate settings and click OK to place the Garment ※ Note: * A Garment can be added by right clicking on the Library's Garment file and using the Add to Workplace menu. **Open or Add settings:** Option | Description ---|--- **Load Type** | Open a new garment file or Add the file additionally. **Content** **(ver 2025.1)** | **Object** | Select the object to load. * Garment * Avatar * Scene and Props * 3D State **Environment** | Select the environment settings to load. * Custom View * Display Settings **Translation** | If you add additional files, you can set the position of the object in the X, Y and Z axis. **X** | Placement long the X axis, relative to the center of the 3D Window. **Y** | Placement long the Y axis, relative to the center of the 3D Window. **Z** | Placement long the Z axis, relative to the center of the 3D Window. **Unit** | Unit for placement. ### ### **New Garment (ver. 12.1)** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ File ▶ New Garment → All existing cloth will be removed and a new "Untitled" project file will be created. ### **Save Garment** #### Save 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Click Main Menu ▶ Save/Save As ▶ **Garment** 2. Set the location and name to save and click the **Save** button. → Save all the garment information. #### Save (Selected) (ver. 2025.1) 1. Select partial garment patterns, or garment patterns and trims in 3D and 2D Windows. 2. Click Main Menu ▶ Save/Save As ▶ **Garment (Selected)** 3. Set the location and name to save and click the **Save** button. → Save the selected garment, or the garment and trim information.****
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions for saving, opening, and managing 3D garment and 2D pattern files in the *.zpac format, enhancing user experience in garment design.

title: Styleline Editing
content: ### Objective Quickly shape patterns in the 3D Window, without the need for previous experience in pattern making. * * * ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Edit Styleline Tools 3D Window ▶ Edit Styleline Tool Dropdown Menu **** ### Operation 1. Load a garment into a scene with an Avatar. 2. Navigate the tool/menu indicated above under "Location". 3. Select a Styleline Editing Tool: Edit Styleline | Select an edit point or place on a curve to skew the pattern shape dynamically. ---|--- Scale Styleline | Select a pattern edge and scale it as a whole. Move Styleline | Select a pattern edge and move it as singular unit which does not skew. Draw Styleline | Draw a new Styleline onto a pattern in the 3D Window. 1. Click on an edge or corner of a pattern piece to begin drawing a new Styleline across it. 2. Click on in the center of the pattern piece to shape the Styleline. 3. Click on another edge or corner of the pattern piece to complete the new Styleline. 4. Manipulate the new Styleline with any of the other Styleline tools. 4. Alter the garment accordingly and watch the patterns update immediately in both the 3D Window and 2D Pattern Window.

title: Requesting Network Software License activation - First Time installation (Linux OS)
content: **[Software License Key for Network Offline] Generate a C2V for First Time Installation - Linux OS** **1\. Install a Run-time Environment on your Linux server following by steps below (step1, step2)** **Step 1.** Unzip aksusbd-8.31.1.tar ([aksusbd-8.31.1](https://s3.amazonaws.com/s3.md.web.upload/newmdweb/helpcenter/installer/aksusbd-8.31.1.tar) **Download**) **Step 2.** As root, open a terminal window and enter the command: **./dinst** Once you are completed with steps above(step1, step2), you’re ready to generate a C2V file for the first time installation of an SL key. **Step 3.** Open a web browser and navigate to ([ACC Page](http://localhost:1947)) **Step 4.** Click on the “Fingerprint” button to create a C2V file. ![pasted_image_0.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438535259545) **Step 5.** Submit your C2V file to this [**page**](https://marvelousdesigner.com/teamconsole/keyupdate/1) (Login with company account is required). If you experience any difficulties, please contact us via support@marvelousdesigner.com **Step 6.** Please refer below to complete a V2C key update. **[Applying a V2C on the server]** 1\. Download the V2C file sent to you from Marvelous Designer Support Team. 2\. Click on the link below to access the ACC Page, then select “Update/Attach” in Options on the left. ([Click here to link ACC Page](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html)) ![v2c_application_1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438535435289) 3\. Click “Choose File” to find and select the downloaded V2C file. ![v2c_application_2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438529660697) 4\. Click “Apply File”. 5\. If the update is successful, the following message will be printed. ![v2c_application_3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438535827353) **[Double checking an updated License Key]** If the License Key Update process is successfully completed, you will be able to double check by following the steps below. 1\. Open a web browser and navigate to [ACC Page](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) 2\. Click Features once you see the key info. ![v2c_application_4.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438530123161) 3\. Make sure the number in the red box has been changed to the correct number. ![v2c_application_5.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438536362905)
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for generating a C2V file and applying a V2C key update for offline software license activation on a Linux server.

title: 3D (Above ver4.2.0)
content: ### Objective Change the default settings of the software in User Settings. Designated settings will become the default after the program is restarted. Shortcut keys, menus, graphics options, view controls, default files, font settings, and other miscellaneous properties can be set in User Settings. In the 3D section, configure settings related to 3D features. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ 3D Main Menu ▶ Settings/Preferences ▶ Preferences ▶ 3D (ver 11) ### Operation 1. Adjust the settings below as needed: Mesh | Set the default mesh setting to Triangle or Quad. ---|--- Arrangement | Default Arrangement Shape Type | Arrange the pattern as curved or flat around the bounding volume of the Avatar when placing patterns around the avatar with arrangement points. Default Arrangement Point Size | Modify the default arrangement point size (radius). For smaller avatars, the default arrangement point size may hinder pattern arrangement, so decrease the size of the arrangement points for efficient pattern arrangement. Sync Fold Arrangement Angle | When using the Fold Arrangement tool, change the selected Internal Line or Pattern Outline's Fold Angle accordingly (ver4.2.0). Gizmo | Unified Gizmo: Select, move, and rotate with a single Gizmo tool. Divided Gizmo: Select (Q), Move (W), Rotate (E) are divided into separate Gizmo tools. The Divided Gizmo tool automatically reassigns the Pin shortcut key from W to P on the keyboard. If P is already in use as a shortcut key, a shortcut key will not be applied to Pin (ver2.5.0).
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for users to customize and set default software settings in the User Settings menu, with a focus on 3D features and arrangement tools.

title: Fabric Texture Normal Map
content: ### Objective Apply Normal Maps to express bumpy surfaces such as twill, corduroy, and leather. ### Location Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric Item ▶ Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Normal Map ### Operation #### Fabric Normal Map 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric Item ▶ Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Normal Map → An intensity value range of -10 to 10 can be adjusted with the scrollbar or entered directly. → Depending on the normal map applied, the visual depth will change as you scroll from negative to positive values. #### Apply Fabric Normal Map Image 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Object Browser ▶ Fabric Tab ▶ Fabric Item ▶ Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Normal Map 2. Click on Open button. 3. Select and load the desired texture image file. → The selected image is now applied. ※ Note : * Although a Normal Map is automatically generated for Fabric textures, it is recommended to use third party solutions to generate more distinctive normal map effects. This feature can also be used to overlay a different texture above the existing texture. The normal map image size can also be adjusted via: Fabric Property Editor ▶ Material ▶ Texture Transformation. * Drag and drop an image file directly from the file browser to the Open icon next to the Normal Map menu in the Property Editor (ver4.0.0). * Drag and drop an image file directly from the file browser to an object in the program, then select the correct map: texture, normal, specular (ver4.0.0).
content_description: Discover how to enhance the realism of fabric textures like twill, corduroy, and leather by applying and adjusting normal maps in the Property Editor.

title: HASP Error Message
content: ## Communication error between local and remote Sentinel HASP License Managers (H0040) ### **Cause of Error** The Server and Client PCs are unable to communicate with each other. ### **Solution** 1\. Type 'services.msc' in the Run window. ![image_1.jpeg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438505080345) 2\. In the Service window that follows, check whether or not the status of the ‘Sentinel LDK License Manager’ is ‘Running’. * If the status is not ‘Running’, right-click and select Start. If the status is ‘Started’, right-click and select Restart. Reboot. ![Image_2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438476878361) 3\. If this does not solve the problem, check both versions of the Server and Client PC’s HASP Drivers. Make sure both versions are the same. You are able to check the version under Diagnostics. ![Image_3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438477089561) 4\. If this does not work, ask your Network Administrator to confirm the Port communication status between the Server and Client. Check whether the 1947 Port is being used by another program. ## ## Feature not found (H0031) ### **Cause of Error** Despite the dongle key has been recognized, the Feature ID of the program and the Feature ID of the dongle key are different. (This occurs when the wrong version of Marvelous Deisnger is installed - i.e. installed the Stand-Alone version for a Network dongle key, and vice versa) ### **Solution** Make sure the correct version of Marvelous Designer is installed. ex> Purchased the Network version, but used the Stand-Alone version's installer. -> Re-install Marvelous Designer using the Network version's installer. ## ## Sentinel HASP key not found (H0007) ### **Cause of Error** * When the HASP Key is not plugged into the PC. * Network Version only: the Client PC does not recognize the Server PC that the dongle key is connected to. * When the HASP Key is recognized, but the Sentinel License Manager service fails to start properly. ### **Solution** Make sure the HASP is connected to the PC. 1. Check the red light of the HASP Key. It should light up when plugged in to the PC. 2. Check whether or not the HASP Key shows up in the [ACC page](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) (refer to the image below) ![Image_4.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438505581465) 3. If the red light or the ACC page does not look equal to the image above, refer to the following manual, reinstall the Sentinel HASP Driver. **[HASP Driver Installation](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358254274585)** ## ## Too many concurrent users (H0038) ### **Cause of Error** When the number of users connected to the program exceeds the maximum allowed number of users. ex> If the maximum number of users (the number of purchased licenses) is 2, and 3 users try to log-in, the last person to attempt a connection will receive an error message. ### **Solution** Check the number of current users via the link below. Connect when one of the current users exit the program. **[ACC Page](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html)** Click Sentinel Keys, on the left. When the Key shows up as the image above, click Sessions, on the right. The following page should display the current user(s). Connect when one of the current users exits the program. If any unauthorized user is connected, click the Disconnect button on the right to log the person out of the program. ## ## Unable to access Sentinel HASP Run-time Environment(H0033) ### **Cause of Error** The HASP Driver has not been properly installed on the PC, or the Driver is damaged. To confirm whether it is properly installed, enter [http://localhost:1947](http://localhost:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) or [http://127.0.0.1:1947](http://127.0.0.1:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) into your web browser, or click on the following link ( [ACC Page](http://127.0.0.1:1947/_int_/ACC_help_index.html) ). If the following page does not look equal to the image below, there is a problem with the Sentinel HASP Driver. ### ![Image_5.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438477525529) **Solution** Refer to the following manual and reinstall the HASP Driver. **[HASP Driver Installation](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358254274585)**
content_description: This web page provides troubleshooting solutions for common communication and licensing errors encountered with Sentinel HASP License Managers in Marvelous Designer.

title: Select All Sewn Patterns (ver. 12.2)
content: ### Objective Makes it easier to select multiple pattern pieces that are connected by sewing relationships. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move tool ▶ Double-click on a pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern tool ▶ Double-click on a pattern 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern tool (right-click on Pattern) ▶ "Select All Sewn (Ctrl + Alt + A)" Main Menu Toolbar ▶ Edit ▶ "Select All Sewn (Ctrl + Alt + A)" ### Operation 1. Follow the dedicated path for the tool found in "Location" above. 2. All patterns that are either directly or indirectly linked by sewing relationships will be selected. ※ Note: \- Select multiple patterns using Shift key. While holding down Shift key, double-click on a specific pattern or use right-click to open the drop-down menu on a pattern piece and pick "Select All Sewn Patterns" to select additional pattern pieces with sewing relationship while maintaining the pre-existing selection. -Piping, binding, buttons, interior shapes, and sewn objects are not selected with the Select All Sewn Patterns feature. -Patterns connected by zippers are selected together with the "Select All Sewn Patterns" feature. -At least 1 pattern piece must be selected for the hotkeys to work.
content_description: This web page provides a streamlined guide for selecting multiple interconnected pattern pieces in sewing software, enhancing efficiency and accuracy in your design process.

title: Symmetrical 3D State (ver. 2024.0)
content: Easily apply the simulation of pattern to its symmetric pattern. ### Steps 1\. This feature only applies to patterns with Symmetrized set. 2\. In the 3D window, right-click on a pattern that is set to symmetrically. 3\. Select the Symmetric Arrangement menu from the right-click pop-up menu. ### End Result The selected pattern is transformed into a simulated version of the opposite Symmetric pattern and is symmetrically arranged relative to the origin of the grid.
content_description: "Transform your symmetrically set patterns into their simulated counterparts with ease using our intuitive 3D interface."

title: Omniverse Connector
content: ## [![940x90-2.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438579593369)](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/) ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Onmiverse Connector (ver. 2025.0) Side Panel Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu Onmiverse Connector (ver. 2025.0) ## ## Feature Overview Through data exchange with the Omniverse platform using USD, collaboration workflows can be accelerated. The following steps are required to use the Omniverse Connector. For more information on NVIDIA and Omniverse, please check out the links below. 1. Create NVIDIA account ([link](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/)) 2. Download and install the Omniverse Launcher ([link](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/omniverse/download/)) 3. Set the Omniverse server ([link](https://docs.omniverse.nvidia.com/prod_nucleus/prod_nucleus/overview.html)) Once done setting up your server in Omniverse Launcher, you can either add the server(Add Server) or join the session(Join Session) in Marvelous Designer. ## Add Server You can add Omniverse Nucleus server in Marvelous Designer. ### Steps Follow the indicated guideline below. Location ![omniverse_server.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438590876441) Marvelous Designer ▶ Omniverse Connector Window ▶ Click on the Omniverse icon ▶ Add Server Enter the server address in the Omniverse Server Connector, and then click on the Add Server button. ### End Result Now you are successfully connected to the server that you entered. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438580043161) ## Create Session / Join Session Create a session for USD files in Omniverse USD Composer, and then you can join that session in Marvelous Designer. ### Step 1. Open a USD file After done connecting to the server, open a USD file which from both Omniverse USD Composer and Marvelous Designer to connect to the session. **Location** **Open a USD file in Marvelous Designer** Marvelous Designer ▶ Omniverse Connector Window ▶ Double-click the Designated Folder \- The files within the folder are displayed in the file list below. \- Double-click or drag & drop the desired file to open it. Also, you can click the right mouse button on the desired file to select Open. **Open a USD file in Omniverse USD Composer** Omniverse USD Composer ▶ Content Tab ▶ Select the Desired Folder ▶ Open the Same File Opened in Marvelous Designer #### End Result The file you opened will be shown in both the 2D and the 3D window, and the list of layers from the file is also displayed in the USD Layer window. ### Step 2. Create Session in Omniverse USD Composer Once you open a USD file, you can create a session in Omniverse USD Composer. * Please Note. Create Session is not available in Marvelous Designer. Location ![omniverse_session_create.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438591178265) Omniverse USD Composer ▶ LIVE Icon Submenu ▶ Create Session \- Enter a session name to create a new session. #### End Result ![session_live_authoring.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438580296473) A session is succesfully created, and you are automatically joined that session with the LIVE icon is activated in Omniverse USD Composer. The Live Session Layer is displayed once you are joined the session. ### Steps 3. Join Session in Marvelous Designer After creating a session in Omniverse USD Composer, you can join the session in Marvelous Designer. **Location** ![marvelous_session_join.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438580550297) Marvelous Designer ▶ Omniverse Connector Window ▶ Click the Omniverse Icon ▶ Join Session \- Select the desired session from the Join Live Session drop-down menu, and click on the Join button. #### End Result Once you are joined the session, the layer from the session is added as a Live type in the USD Layer window. The layer will have the same name as the Live Session Layer in Omniverse USD Composer, and be set to the Authoring Layer. ![session_live_authoring2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438591739033) ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438580043161) **Live Indicator** When joining a session, you can find the live indicator in both Marvelous Designer and Omniverse USD Composer. ![omniverse_live.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438581083417) Marvelous Designer ▶ Omniverse Connector Window ▶ The Live indicator appears on the Omniverse icon **Session Participants (in Marvelous Designer)** ![omniverse_session_member_.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438592147481) Marvelous Designer ▶ Omniverse Connector Window ▶ Click on the Refresh Participants button right next to the Server. The session participants icon appears on the left of the Omniverse icon. Hover your mouse on the icon to see the participants and their software information. **Session Participants (in Omniverse USD Composer)** ![omniverse_session_member2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438592384153) Omniverse USD Composer ▶ The name of the participant appears on the right of the Live icon The session participants icon appears next to the Live icon. Hover your mouse on the icon to see the participants and their software information. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438580043161) ## Session in Progress ### Export files from Marvelous Designer to Omniverse USD Composer When a session in Omniverse USD Composer is connected in Marvelous Designer, you can export your work in Marvelous Designer to Omniverse USD Composer through the Export to USD Layer feature. The way Omniverse USD Composer updates the work depends on the type of USD layer (USD, LIVE) that the Authoring Layer is set to. ### Steps ### Where the Live Session Layer is set as the Authoring Layer ![usd_live_authoring.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438581715097) Select desired clothing or trims and click on Export to USD Layer from the right mouse button pop-up menu. #### End Result \- The changes of the session layer is directly reflected to the Omniverse USD Composer. \- If there is no Prim with the same name on the same Prim Path in Omniverse USD Composer, add a new Prim (Append). \- If there is a Prim with the same name in the Prim Path you set for export in Omniverse USD Composer, the changes will be overwritten on that Prim. ### Where a USD Layer is set as the Authoring Layer ![usd_usd_authoring.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438592802457) Select desired clothing or trims and click on Export to USD Layer from the right mouse button pop-up menu. #### End Result \- The selected are exported to the USD file, but not directly reflected to the Omniverse USD Composer. \- To see these changes in the Omniverse USD Composer, click the FETCH button when the 'Base USD files have been changed' pop-up appears. ![usd_fetch.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438582081689) \- If there is no Prim with the same name on the same Prim Path in Omniverse USD Composer, add a new Prim (Append). \- If there is a Prim with the same name in the Prim Path you set for export in Omniverse USD Composer, the changes will be overwritten on that Prim. ### * How to update the changes from Omniverse USD Composer to Marvelous Designer Marvelous Designer cannot directly reflect any changes from Omniverse USD Composer. If you need to use a USD file which is modified from the Omniverse USD Composer, the file should be reimported to Marvelous Designer. Merge the USD changes Omniverse USD Composer, and then reimport the file in Marvelous Designer. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438580043161) ## Leave Session You can leave the session that you're in both Marvelous Designer and Omniverse USD Composer. ### Steps #### Leave Session in Marvelous Designer Location ![omniverse_leave2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438582359065) Marvelous Designer ▶ Omniverse Connector Window ▶ Click the Omniverse Icon ▶ Leave Session \- Click on the Leave button when Information pop-up window appears. #### End Result The current session ends and the Live mark disappears from the Omniverse icon. The list of session participants disappears. #### Leave Session in Omniverse USD Composer Location ![omniverse_leave.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438626917273) Omniverse USD Composer ▶ Live Icon Submenu ▶ Leave Session \- Click on the Leave button in the Leave Session window. #### End Result The current session ends and the Live status is changed to deactivated. The list of session participants disappears. * Please try out this **[USD sample file](https://s3.marvelousdesigner.com/newmdweb/helpcenter/manual/KoiFish_USD.zip) **we created with Marvelous Designer and see how the new USD support can benefit your workflow. You can find step by step **[tutorial](https://youtu.be/r7AfPVd8WG4)** for how to export this USD file from Marvelous Designer.
content_description: This webpage serves as a comprehensive guide for using the Omniverse Connector in Marvelous Designer, detailing setup, session management, and file export processes to enhance collaborative workflows through USD data exchange.

title: ANIMATION MODE: Record Animation
content: ### Objective Record garment animation. ※ Note: Follow the link; [Process of Making Garment Animation](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115000560428) for your reference on creating garment animation in details. ### Location Animation Mode ▶ Animation Editor ▶ Record ### Operation 1\. Follow the indicated guideline below: Animation Mode ▶ Animation Editor ▶ Record → Simulation turns on automatically and it is now being recorded in frames. → If a Transition Animation is created, the recording automatically stops at the end of the Transition Animation frame and starts again (ver2.5.0). ※ Note: Transition Animation is auto-generated animation tool which automatically generates for stabilizing transition when the original Avatar pose is different to the first pose in the motion file. Once the garment and avatar arrive in a new position, it is no longer in need therefore the recording automatically stops for you to delete this unnecessary part. The Transition Animation for default avatars of version10 is not compatible with the previous versions. 2\. Once the Avatar's motion ends, the recording automatically stops. To stop the recording while it is in process, click the Pause button. **Copy Frame** The feature is to create assets for Dynamic Wrinkle. (ver. 5.1.445) \- After recording an animation of a garment and copy /paste on designated frame.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide for recording garment animations using the Animation Editor in CLO 3D, including essential features and operational steps for successful execution.

title: Transform Point/Segment
content: ### ### ### ### ### Objective Transform a Pattern by scaling or rotating its point and segment. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Point/Segment 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern tool (hold down the button)▶ Transform Point/Segment ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Transform Point/Segment 2D Toolbar ▶ Edit Pattern tool (hold down the button)▶ Transform Point/Segment 2. Select the point/segment to be transformed. → The selected point/segment is highlighted in yellow and the surrounding marquee box appears. → The Transform pattern tool's selection box can now select patterns no matter the area it covers; by holding CTRL and clicking and dragging your mouse. (ver. 2024.0) 3. Move, scale, or rotate the selected point/segment. → The Pattern is transformed as the selected points/segments are edited.
content_description: This web page provides step-by-step instructions for transforming a 2D pattern by scaling or rotating its points and segments using the Edit Pattern tool.

title: Complete Nonlinear Simulation
content: ### Objective This function allows more accurate Simulation on fabric stretch (ver3.0.0). It is especially effective for longer Garments. ※ Note: This is available from ver3.0.0 onward. ### Location 3D Garment Window ▶ Right-click Pop-up Menu ▶ Simulation Properties ▶ Property Editor ▶ Nonlinear Simulation ### Operation Follow the indicated guideline below and check the Nonlinear Simulation On: 3D Garment Window ▶ Simulation Property Editor ▶ Preset ▶ Complete (Nonlinear) → Fabric strength and elongation are now being simulated more accurately.
content_description: Enhance your garment simulations with improved accuracy for fabric stretch in longer garments using the Nonlinear Simulation feature available in version 3.0.0 and onward.

title: Flip Normal
content: ### Objective Easily flip the wrong/right side of Fabric before or after draping. Sew Patterns as desired first and flip the fabric surface at last to save time. ### Location Garment Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Pattern ▶ Flip Normal ### Operation 1. Select Select/Move tool. 2. Select a Pattern to flip. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Garment Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Pattern ▶ Flip Normal → The selected pattern's fabric surface is now being flipped over. ※ Note: Fold Angle value also gets flipped when flipping normal (ver2.4.0).
content_description: This web page provides a quick guide for flipping the fabric surface of a pattern in Fabric software, enabling users to efficiently adjust their designs before finalizing their draping.

title: 2D Pattern View Controls
content: ### Objective #### Zoom to Selected Zoom in to the selected Pattern at your convenience. #### Zoom Extents All Zoom in or out the 2D window to see all Patterns. #### Smart Panning The 2D window is going to pan automatically following the mouse cursor. ### Location #### Zoom to Selected Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Focus Zoom Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Zoom to Selected Click (on Pattern) ▶ F key on the keyboard #### Zoom Extents All Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D window) ▶ Zoom Extents All #### Smart Panning Main Menu ▶ Applicable Select/Edit Tool 3D/ 2D Toolbar ▶ Applicable Select/Edit Tool ※ Note: #### Applicable Select/Edit Tool: Tools used to create pattern/internal shapes, create/edit sewing lines, and create/edit topstitches have smart panning function. ### Operation #### Zoom to Selected 1. Navigate to the 2D Toolbar and select the Transform Pattern or the Edit Pattern. 2. Left click on the pattern to be zoomed in. 3. Follow the indicated guideline below: Display ▶ Viewpoint ▶ Focus Zoom Right Click Pop-Up Menu (on Pattern) ▶ Zoom to Selected Left Click (on Pattern) ▶ F key on the keyboard →The 2D window is scaled to the selected pattern and the 2D window can be controlled on the basis of the selected Pattern. #### Zoom Extents All 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Right-Click Pop-Up Menu (on 2D window) ▶ Zoom Extents All → The 2D window is scaled to show all Patterns in the 2D window. #### Smart Panning 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Applicable Select/Edit Tool 3D/ 2D Toolbar ▶ Applicable Select/Edit Tool →The 2D Window is going to pan automatically following the mouse cursor.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for utilizing zoom and smart panning features in a 2D design interface to enhance navigation and focus on selected patterns.

title: Other (Above ver4.2.0)
content: ### Objective Change the default settings of the software in User Settings. Designated settings will become the default after the program is restarted. Shortcut keys, menus, graphics options, view controls, default files, font settings, and other miscellaneous properties can be set in User Settings. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ Others Main Menu ▶ Settings/Preferences ▶ Preferences ▶ Others (ver 11) ### Operation 1. Adjust the settings below as needed: MetaData | Show Option to Save MetaData | Turn on the 'Show Option to Save MetaData', the options appears when saving your project or garment and metadata file together is shown again. ---|---|--- Modular Configurator | Maintain Block Selections with Same Name | In Modular Mode, pattern selection is maintained when Blocks have the same name. Maintain Fabric Properties for Patterns with Same Name | In Modular Mode, fabric application is maintained when Blocks have the same name.
content_description: This web page guides users on how to customize and save their default software settings through the User Settings menu to enhance their experience and streamline operations.

title: Slash & Spread
content: ### ### ### ### Objective Slash and spread a Pattern using an Internal Line inside the Pattern (ver2.4.0). ### Location Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Slash & Spread 2D Toolbar ▶ Slash & Spread ### Operation #### Slash & Spread 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Slash & Spread 2D Toolbar ▶ Slash & Spread 2. Click on the Pattern outline to draw a Slash Line. Drag the mouse as the Slash Line follows along the mouse cursor. Click again on the Pattern outline to complete the Slash Line. Or, Click on the Internal Line within the Pattern to set it as a Slash Line (ver2.5.0). 3. Choose the side of the Pattern to be rotated. → The selected side of the Pattern is highlighted in yellow. 4. Drag the mouse cursor towards the Pattern should be rotated. → The preview of the edited pattern appears. 5. When the desired shape is achieved, click on the 2D window to complete Slash & Spread. #### Slash & Spread with Distance and Angle 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Edit ▶ Slash & Spread 2D Toolbar ▶ Slash & Spread 2. Click on the Pattern outline to draw a Slash Line. Drag the mouse as the Slash Line follows along the mouse cursor. Click again on the Pattern outline to complete the Slash Line. Or, click on the Internal Line within the Pattern to set it as a Slash Line (ver2.5.0). 3. Right click on the 2D window to access the pop-up menu. → The Spread window appears. 4. Enter the desired values for Distance and Angle. Distance | Set how much in length the selected side of the Pattern spreads. ---|--- Angle | Set the angle the selected side of the Pattern spreads. 5. Click OK to complete Slash & Spread. ※ Note: * When selecting an Internal Line as a Slash Line, the side closer to the mouse cursor spreads. * Click on the slash line to spread patterns on both sides. (ver MD10) * The shape of the Pattern can be previewed when closing the Pattern. Also, the Pattern Outline is smoothened into a natural curve. (ver MD10)
content_description: This web page provides a detailed guide on how to use the "Slash & Spread" feature in version 2.4.0 and 2.5.0 of our software to manipulate 2D patterns effectively.

title: 2D (Above ver4.2.0)
content: ### Objective Change the default settings of the software in User Settings. Designated settings will become the default after the program is restarted. Shortcut keys, menus, graphics options, view controls, default files, font settings, and other miscellaneous properties can be set in User Settings. In the 2D section, configure settings related to 2D features. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ User Settings ▶ 2D Main Menu ▶ Settings/Preferences ▶ Preferences ▶ 2D (ver 11) ### Operation 1. Adjust the settings below as needed: Pattern | Default Particle Distance | Set the default particle distance when creating patterns. ---|---|--- Automatically Offset 2D Patterns when Cut | Toggle the option to offset 2D patterns when the Cut function is used, making it easier to work with UV export (ver3.2.0).
content_description: This web page provides guidance on adjusting and configuring default settings in the software's User Settings, specifically focusing on 2D features to enhance user experience and workflow.

title: Button Right-Click Menus
content: ### Objective Change status of buttons as desired. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Button) Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Button) ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Button) Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ Pop-up Menu (Right-click 3D/2D Button) 2. Right-click on the button to edit. → Button related pop-up menu appears. Pop-up Menu | Description ---|--- Reset 3D Position | Reset to location of pre-simulation. Copy | Copy the selected button. Paste | Paste the selected button. Mirror Paste (Position Only) | Mirror paste the position of the selected button. Delete | Delete the selected button. Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern | Duplicate the selected button to its symmetric pattern. Activate/Deactivate | Activate or deactivate the selected button. Freeze/Unfreeze | Freeze or unfreeze the selected button. Set Number of Sewing Layers | Set the number of sewing layers for the selected button. After setting the Number of Sewing Layers, use the Select/Move Button tool to adjust buttons' locations on each Patterns. Flip | Move the selected button to the opposite side. Align | Align selected buttons based on the selected options. Distribute | Distribute selected buttons horizontally or vertically with same intervals
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for modifying the status and positioning of buttons in a 3D environment using the Select/Move tool and associated pop-up menu options.
